Public contract supports README claims: repair existing Python processor and journal; event-time tenant+user half-open sessions; --input tie-break vs --feed file order; exit 2 before journal/output touch on bad CLI; watermark never steps backward; empty input does not advance watermark; fail closed to rejects; last_run/ops-report from warehouse catalog; leave warehouse click dump alone; catalog session_gap overlay in processor.json.

Difficulty matches the concrete-bottleneck pattern (plausible partial fixes that still fail) rather than generic multi-component filler. Solution is invariant-focused, not a file-by-file diff. Verification names scenario purpose without claiming comprehensive/robust coverage.
Aligns with human difficulty/solution/verification pairs (reasoning trap, authoritative invariants, scenario families that rule out wrong classes) and avoids stock AI documentation phrases.

Section 12 requires human README covering difficulty rationale, solution approach, and verification approach; README supplies those without agent-facing instruction copy or oracle internals beyond naming solution/solve.sh as the Harbor reference entrypoint.
